ledger.homeUse: Food eaten from your own store
report.farmIncome.why: What your crops and fruit earned this season: sold {sold}, eaten at home {homeUse}. Food your family ate from the store counts too: it's grocery money you didn't spend. Accountants call this revenue.
report.farmCosts.why: Seed {seed}, fertiliser and spray {fert}, hired help {wages}, wear and tear on buildings {depreciation}, carting and market fees {transport}. Inputs count when used, not when bought: buying ahead is a swap of cash for stock.
report.farmProfit: Did the farm pay for itself?
report.farmProfit.why: Money from your harvests minus what farming cost you: {profit}. Above zero means the farm paid its way this season. The Hamlet needs one such season. Accountants call this farm profit.
report.otherIncome.why: Day labour on neighbours' farms {dayLabour}, gains on things you sold {gains}.
report.household.why: Food and basics on the {plan} plan {living}, medicine {health}. Paid at the start of the season and counted day by day.
report.finance.why: What borrowing cost this season: {interest}. A loan helps only if what it buys earns more than this.
report.other.why: Trees removed or spent, land sold below what you paid: {loss}.
report.netResult.why: Everything earned minus everything spent: {net}. This is your profit for the season.
report.cashFlow.why: Cash can move differently from profit: {upfront} was paid now for next season's living costs or wages, so cash fell by more than the costs.
report.netWorth: What you own minus what you owe
report.netWorth.why: Cash {cash}, prepaid {prepaid}, land at today's price {land}, buildings {buildings}, trees {trees}, goods in store {goods}, minus loans {loans}. Land and goods are at market value; your books show them at cost ({bookEquity}).
report.homeUse.why: Home-grown food paid {homeUse} of your living costs; your garden gave {garden} of it.

forecast.subtitle: Today's forecast is sure; tomorrow's and the next day's are likely
why.fertility.title: Soil fertility
why.fertility.effect: What it does to every harvest here
why.fertility.cropuse: Taken out by crops this season
why.fertility.lentils: Lentils fed the soil this season
why.fertility.fallow: Rest while the field lay empty
why.fertility.lesson: Every crop takes something out. Compost, lentils and rest put it back; chemical fertiliser lifts one harvest but wears the soil.
why.moisture.title: Soil moisture
why.moisture.wetter: {weather} weather adds this much water each hour
why.moisture.drier: {weather} weather dries this much out each hour
why.moisture.drainage: Past a point, {soil} soil drains the extra water away hour by hour.
why.moisture.well: The well keeps this acre at least at
why.moisture.lesson: Too dry or too wet, a crop gives less. A well acre never gets too dry.
why.soil.title: Soil for crops
why.soil.shade: Shade from trees at the field's edge
why.soil.all: All together, on every harvest here
why.soil.lesson: The soil sets what every crop on this acre can give.
why.timeLeft.title: {crop}: time left
why.timeLeft.lesson: Weather and care change how much you harvest, never how long a crop takes.
why.care.title: Care of your fields
why.care.effect: What it does to every harvest
why.care.cap: Care beyond what the crops need adds a little, up to a tenth more.
why.care.lesson: Short of hands, every field suffers a little. Hire help or sow less.
why.water.title: Water
why.water.effect: What it has done to this harvest so far
why.water.lesson: Sow where the moisture suits the crop, or on a well acre.
why.weather.title: Weather
why.weather.sofar: The weather so far, on this harvest
why.weather.lesson: One bad hour costs little: the harvest feels the weather over the whole of its growth.
why.yield.title: Harvest of {crop}
why.yield.base: A full {crop} harvest here (this sowing's share of {season} kg an acre a season)
why.yield.seedSaved: Saved seed (it weakens a little each season)
why.yield.cap: The most an acre can give
why.yield.lesson: The weakest cause hurts most: lift it first.
why.spoils.title: Before it starts to spoil
why.spoils.grace: A ready crop waits safely for
why.spoils.lesson: Collect within three days, or sell straight from the field.
why.pests.title: Pests
why.pests.repeats: Times this crop followed itself here
why.pests.wet: Wet weather while it grows raises the risk.
why.pests.sprayed: You sprayed: the damage is limited.
why.pests.lesson: Change crops on an acre: pests build up when the same crop follows itself.
why.landPrice.title: Price of this land
why.landPrice.lesson: Land pays back over many seasons: about 8 to 15 seasons of an acre's profit.
why.resale.title: If you sold it quickly
why.resale.lesson: Selling in a hurry costs a fifth of the price.
why.garden.lesson: The kitchen garden feeds the family a little every day.
why.gardenCrop.title: {crop}: ready in
why.treeMatures.title: {tree}: grown in
why.treeMatures.fruits: Once grown, it fruits in its seasons, batch after batch.
why.payback.title: Has it paid for itself?
why.payback.lesson: A tree costs now and pays for years: that's an investment.
why.sapling.title: {tree} sapling
why.sapling.planting: The price includes digging and planting it.
why.cash.title: Cash
why.cash.quiet: No money in or out yet today.
why.cash.lesson: Cash is not profit: paying ahead or buying stock moves cash without being a cost yet.
why.store.title: Your store
why.store.room: The hut holds a fixed weight. What doesn't fit waits where it is or sells to the trader.
why.store.lesson: Sell before the store fills, or a harvest has nowhere to go.
why.price.index: Prices this year (they rise a little each season)
why.traderPrice.title: What the trader pays for {good}
why.traderPrice.lesson: The trader buys at the valley's price less the carting, up to what he can take each day.
why.marketPrice.title: {good} on the village market
why.marketPrice.floor: It never stays far below what the trader pays
why.marketPrice.ceiling: Or far above what bringing it in costs
why.marketPrice.offered: What's on offer, yours included, pushes the price down.
why.marketPrice.demand: With nothing on offer, the price sits at the valley's.
why.marketPrice.lesson: Offer a little at a time: a glut sinks the price to the trader's.
why.traderRoom.title: The trader can still take
why.traderRoom.lesson: His room comes back each morning.
why.spoilage.title: Spoils by tomorrow
why.spoilage.offer: Stock you've offered at the market spoils last.
why.spoilage.lesson: Grain keeps; potatoes, fruit and greens don't. Sell the quick spoilers first.
why.input.title: {good} in store
why.input.use: It counts as a cost when you sow or spray with it.
why.input.lesson: Buying ahead swaps cash for stock: your profit isn't touched until you use it.
why.inputPrice.title: {good} costs
why.inputPrice.lesson: Seed is dearer at sowing time: buying ahead saves money.
why.mandi.title: The mandi trip
why.mandi.0: At the town mandi your goods fetch the valley's price when the trolley gets back, {hours} hours after it leaves.
why.mandi.1: The commission agent keeps {pct} of the sale.
why.mandi.2: A tractor-trolley is hired for the trip; it carries up to {kg}.
why.mandi.3: Going takes half an hour of your day, once a day at most.
why.mandi.4: The village trader pays less, but at once and with no trip.
why.mandi.lesson: A trip pays when the load is big enough to cover the trolley.
why.netWorth.title: What you own minus what you owe
why.netWorth.book: In your books (land and goods at what they cost)
why.netWorth.lesson: Net worth grows when what you earn beats what you spend and owe.
why.credit.title: {lender}: you can borrow
why.credit.base: Lends anyone in the village up to
why.credit.land: Land you bought counts for ({pct} of its value)
why.credit.inherited: Your family's land can never be pledged.
why.credit.tooLow: Your score is below what this lender accepts.
why.credit.lesson: Borrow only for what earns more than the interest.
why.loan.title: {lender}: still owed
why.loan.bullet: Interest each season; the whole loan back with the last payment.
why.loan.instalments: A part of the loan back each season, with its interest.
why.loan.lesson: A missed payment costs late interest and your score.
why.borrow.title: Paying back over
why.borrow.lesson: A longer term means smaller payments but more interest in all.
why.seasonSoFar.title: This season so far
why.seasonSoFar.close: The books close at the season's end, with its report.
why.seasonSoFar.lesson: A season's living costs are paid at its start, so profit counts the farm alone.
why.calendar.title: The calendar
why.calendar.clock: The game's clock matches your phone's: the farm keeps working while the app is closed.
why.calendar.away: Away longer than {hours} hours, the farm waits for you.
why.calendar.lesson: One hour here is about a day in the valley.
why.forecast.title: How sure is this?
why.forecast.runs: Weather comes in runs: calm weather lasts, storms pass in an hour or two.
why.forecast.lesson: Plan on today's forecast; keep a margin for the days after.
why.saved.title: Saving
why.saved.when: The game saves every hour, a few seconds after your last tap, and when you leave the app.
why.saved.backups: It keeps backups, so a crash never costs more than an hour.
why.labour.title: Your work today
why.labour.lesson: Eat well and rest: a tired, hungry founder gets less done.
why.health.title: Health
why.health.cold: No warm clothes in Winter takes
why.health.sick: The lower your health, the likelier a sick day.
why.health.lesson: Medicine helps once a day; good food helps every day.
why.fatigue.title: Tiredness
why.fatigue.lesson: Long days add up; a rest day takes tiredness away.
why.diet.title: {plan} food plan
why.diet.food: Home-grown food can pay this much of it
why.diet.paid: Paid at the start of the season.
why.diet.lesson: Cheap food costs work: you get less done each day.
why.hours.title: {option}
why.dayLabour.title: Day labour pays about
why.dayLabour.fields: Those hours come off your own fields.
why.dayLabour.lesson: Day labour is sure money; your own fields may earn more.
why.medicine.title: Medicine
why.medicine.once: One dose a day helps; more doesn't.
why.hire.title: Hiring day labourers
why.hire.care: Their hours join yours in caring for the fields.
why.hire.leave: They go home when the day ends.
why.handSkill.title: Skill
why.handSkill.grows: Skill grows with every season worked.
why.handSkill.lesson: A hand who stays gets better.
why.handHours.title: A hand's work
why.handHours.skill: A more skilled hand gets more done in a day.
why.handHours.acre: About 3 hours a day tends an acre of wheat.
why.handWage.title: Wage a season
why.handWage.paid: Paid at the start of each season, for the season ahead.
why.handWage.lesson: A hand pays when the acres they tend earn more than the wage.
why.handLapse.title: Unpaid wage
why.handLapse.what: The contract lapsed: the hand waits a while for the wage before leaving.
why.handLapse.backPay: Renewing now pays what is owed.
why.handPrepaid.title: Wage paid ahead
why.handPrepaid.what: The part of this season's wage not yet worked.
why.handPrepaid.lesson: Paying ahead is cash out now; the cost counts day by day.
why.hut.title: A hand's hut
why.hut.what: A hand needs a hut in the labour quarters.
why.applicant.title: What you know of them
why.applicant.range: Until you talk, you only know their skill roughly.
why.orderMin.title: Lowest price
why.orderMin.what: Your hand won't sell below this at the market.
why.orderMin.floor: Below the trader's price, the trader buys anyway.
why.free.title: Labourers free today
why.free.pool: Neighbouring villages send a few each day.
why.away.title: While you were away
why.away.Ready: Crops, beds and trees that ripened while you were away wait for you to collect them.
why.away.Sales: Your offers at the market sold hour by hour; the trader bought at his price.
why.away.DayLabour: You worked on neighbours' farms as planned.
why.away.HomeUse: Your family ate from the store: food you didn't have to buy.
why.away.Spoiled: Goods lose a little each day in the store; a ready crop starts to spoil after three days.
why.away.Pests: Pests found a crop. Spray it to limit the damage.
why.away.Sick: On a sick day you rest.
why.away.Seasons: A season closed: its report shows how the farm did.
why.away.Index: Prices rise a little each season.
why.away.People: Your hands worked through their orders.
why.away.lesson: The farm keeps going while you're away, for up to three days.
why.report.farmCosts: Inputs count when used, not when bought.
why.report.household: Living costs come before anything else.
why.report.finance: A loan helps only if what it buys earns more than this.
why.report.other: Losses on things sold or gone.
why.report.netResult: This is your profit for the season.
account.CropSales: Crops sold and eaten at home
account.FruitSales: Fruit sold and eaten at home
why.gardenSeason.title: Picked from this bed this season
why.gardenSeason.total: A bed gives in a season
why.gardenSeason.rest: Once it has given its season's worth, the bed rests until the next season.
why.order.title: {name}'s order
why.order.what: An order is a job your hand does by themselves: sow, harvest, pick and sell.
why.order.hour: A hand does one thing an hour on each order.
why.order.never: A hand never undoes a crop you sowed yourself.
why.post.title: Sending word for a hand
why.post.what: Word goes round the neighbouring villages: for a few days people come asking for work more often.
why.post.above: Offering above the usual wage brings better, surer people, who ask for more.
